headline: WhatsApp now allows direct iPad sign-ups and revamps CarPlay/Android Auto experience
summary: WhatsApp users can now register directly from their iPad without linking to a phone. The app also gets significantly enhanced Apple CarPlay and Android Auto integrations, along with new media and document features.
details: WhatsApp is rolling out a suite of new features, including the ability to sign up directly from an iPad and revamped Apple CarPlay/Android Auto experiences. This push aims to make the Meta-owned app a more complete cross-device communication platform.

Users can now register for a WhatsApp account directly through the iPad app, without having to link to a primary phone. While a phone number is still required to receive the one-time passcode during registration, the app will then function as a standalone account.

The integration with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto has been significantly improved. Previously limited to composing messages and placing calls, users can now hear and reply to messages, view their call history, and access favorite contacts directly in their vehicle.
Additional features include the ability to share a song straight from Apple Music or Spotify to WhatsApp Status. This allows users to express themselves and make their status more unique.

WhatsApp also now makes it possible to open PDFs directly within the app on web and desktop without downloading them. Once opened, users can make lightweight edits such as highlighting and annotating right within the chat.

These updates add to a growing list of recent WhatsApp features. The company recently launched usernames for sharing profiles without phone numbers, and a WhatsApp Plus subscription plan for extra customization and insights.

headline_marked: [[Cult social robot Jibo gets AI wearable successor]] iKairos, raising $29M in funding
headline: Cult social robot Jibo gets AI wearable successor iKairos, raising $29M in funding
summary: The new modular AI device, iKairos, combines a neck-worn wearable with a home dock, aiming to provide context-aware assistance by understanding your life, not just prompts. Lingverse, the company behind it, has secured $29 million in pre-A funding.
details: Jibo, the social robot that ceased operations in 2019, is getting a spiritual successor called iKairos. This new modular AI device from Lingverse embraces the trend for AI wearables while also being useful at home, securing $29 million in pre-A funding.

iKairos is designed to continuously observe both the user and their surroundings, creating the context that current AI often lacks. This allows it to act as a personal AI guardian, proactively adapting to and working around your lifestyle.

The wearable component is expected to be neck-worn and feature a camera. Lingverse addresses privacy concerns by including a physical cover over the lens, ensuring users know when it's recording. At home, the wearable attaches to a dock, reminiscent of the original Jibo.

The AI's core function is to provide context-aware advice and anticipate user needs. The more it learns about an individual, the better it can offer timely reminders and suggestions, unlocking new experiences.

Jiawei Gu, a former board member and investor in Jibo, is leading Lingverse with the backing of the original Jibo team. Lingverse aims to build upon Jibo's legacy, incorporating lessons learned from the previous device's limitations as a purely home-based system.

Lingverse has opened a waitlist on its website, with pre-orders anticipated to begin between July and September this year. Specific pricing and final availability details for iKairos have not yet been announced.
